boards.school_name: The University of Texas at Austin
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission activities on and beside UT Austin’s campus, using public art, galleries, and museums with documented free access.

cards.title: Walk around Clock Knot
cards.subtitle: Landmarks public art, near CPE and ETC
cards.notes: Meet at the grassy berm and circle the steel sculpture together; its shifting angles read differently from each side.
cards.short_summary: A large outdoor sculpture for a quick campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmarks states that its outdoor works are always accessible and free to the public; Clock Knot is on the berm between CPE and ETC.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor Landmarks works are always accessible and free; observe the work from public paths and do not climb it.

cards.title: Look up at Monochrome for Austin
cards.subtitle: Northwest corner of 24th Street and Speedway
cards.notes: Use the corner as a meetup point, then trace the cluster of recycled boats and canoes from across the sidewalk.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Landmarks sculpture made from 70 aluminum boats and canoes.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmarks identifies Monochrome for Austin at 24th Street and Speedway; outdoor Landmarks works are always accessible and free to the public.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor Landmarks works are always accessible and free; view from public sidewalks and paths.

cards.title: See Sentinel IV in the courtyard
cards.subtitle: Anna Hiss Gymnasium Courtyard
cards.notes: Pause in the courtyard to view Simone Leigh’s bronze figure, then compare its silhouette from several public vantage points.
cards.short_summary: A bronze Landmarks sculpture in the Anna Hiss Gymnasium Courtyard.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmarks lists Sentinel IV in the Anna Hiss Gymnasium Courtyard; its outdoor works are always accessible and free to the public.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor Landmarks works are always accessible and free; remain in publicly accessible courtyard areas.

cards.title: Circle Amaryllis
cards.subtitle: East of the Texas Science & Natural History Museum
cards.notes: Walk a slow loop around Tony Smith’s black steel form and compare which geometric faces appear from each angle.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor geometric steel sculpture beside the science museum.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmarks places Amaryllis east of the Texas Science & Natural History Museum; outdoor Landmarks works are always accessible and free to the public.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor Landmarks works are always accessible and free; view from surrounding public paths.

cards.title: Reserve a Skyspace visit
cards.subtitle: Student Activity Center rooftop
cards.notes: Book a free slot, arrive together, and spend time beneath the oculus observing the changing sky and programmed light.
cards.short_summary: James Turrell’s campus Skyspace offers free reservations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Color Inside welcomes the campus community and public, and its reservation page describes reservations as free.
cards.source_title: The Color Inside | University of Texas
cards.access_notes: Free reservation required for sunset viewing; daytime visits are available subject to the site’s posted access guidance.

cards.title: Browse the Visual Arts Center
cards.subtitle: College of Fine Arts, UT Austin
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition, meet in the gallery, and take time to discuss one work that catches each person’s attention.
cards.short_summary: A UT gallery with exhibitions and public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin’s Department of Art and Art History states that the Visual Arts Center is always free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Community Overview | Department of Art and Art History
cards.access_notes: Always free and open to the public; confirm current gallery hours before traveling.

cards.entity_name: Dolph Briscoe Center for American History
cards.title: Browse the Briscoe Center galleries
cards.subtitle: Sid Richardson Hall Unit 2, 2300 Red River Street
cards.notes: Meet in the ground-floor exhibit spaces and choose an artifact, photograph, or document to discuss before you leave.
cards.short_summary: Free public exhibits and reading-room access on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Briscoe Center lists free admission for its galleries, classrooms, and public spaces.
cards.source_title: Research and Collections | Dolph Briscoe Center for American History
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; exhibits are listed Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m., with holiday closures posted by the center.

cards.title: Visit the Blanton galleries
cards.subtitle: 200 East Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard
cards.notes: Bring a valid UT Austin ID, pick one gallery to explore, and regroup afterward to swap observations about the art.
cards.short_summary: UT students can enter the Blanton’s galleries without admission cost.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blanton lists UT-Austin ID admission as free and states that admission is free for all UT students, staff, and faculty.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Blanton Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Free with UT-Austin ID; verify current gallery hours and special closures on the museum’s visit page.

cards.title: Explore the science museum
cards.subtitle: Texas Memorial Museum building, 2400 Trinity Street
cards.notes: Bring a valid UT ID, choose an exhibit section, and compare a favorite specimen or object before heading out.
cards.short_summary: UT ID holders receive free admission to campus natural-history exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin’s catalog states that Texas Science & Natural History Museum admission is free for UT students, staff, and faculty with valid UT ID.
cards.source_title: Texas Science & Natural History Museum | UT Austin Catalog
cards.access_notes: Free with valid UT ID; the museum lists Tuesday–Saturday and Sunday public hours, with Monday closure.

cards.title: Take a Landmarks outdoor art walk
cards.subtitle: UT Austin main campus
cards.notes: Open Landmarks’ mobile tour, choose a route, and make a no-rush loop between several sculptures using public walkways.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided way to connect multiple outdoor campus artworks.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmarks provides self-guided mobile tours, and UT Austin states that Landmarks’ outdoor art is always available and free to the public.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor works are always available and free; indoor stops, if added, depend on each building’s operating hours.
